# ceph/s3-tests node IDs that are expected to FAIL.
#
# This is the gate, and it runs the other way round from an allow-list: CI runs
# the *whole* suite on every pull request and fails if anything outside this
# file fails — or if anything inside it passes.
#
# The second half is what keeps the file honest. An allow-list only ever grows:
# a test that starts passing stays invisible until someone runs the suite by
# hand and promotes it, and a test that starts failing outside the list is never
# noticed at all. Here both show up on the pull request that caused them, and
# the list can only shrink.
#
# So: when a change makes a test pass, delete its line in the same change. Do
# not add lines to make CI green — a new line means a regression you are
# choosing to keep, and it needs a reason next to it.
#
# Every line is one of:
#   * a feature we have not built yet (see STATUS.md for the clusters);
#   * a scope decision published in COMPATIBILITY.md;
#   * an upstream test no server passes, or one that encodes RGW behaviour.
#
# Skipped tests appear in neither list: 94 of them need a Ceph client extension
# or a storage class this deployment does not have.
#
# Regenerate wholesale after an S3TESTS_REF bump:
#   go run ./scripts/s3tests update --report s3tests.xml --report headers.xml
#

s3tests/functional/test_s3.py::test_versioning_stack_delete_merkers

# SSE-KMS: refused rather than ignored (#124, and #133 for the feature).
#
# These thirteen passed until server-side encryption was implemented, and
# they passed for a bad reason: x-amz-server-side-encryption: aws:kms was
# accepted and then ignored, so the object was written in the clear while
# the client had been told its request was honored. Each test only checks
# that the round-trip returns what it wrote, which a server storing
# plaintext does perfectly well.
#
# An algorithm this server does not implement is now refused, so they fail
# honestly. That is a smaller passing count and a server that no longer
# claims an encryption it is not performing — SSE-KMS needs a key service
# and is out of scope (#133).
#
# test_sse_kms_no_key came off the list in the same change: it asserts that
# requesting KMS without a key fails, which is now true.
s3tests/functional/test_s3.py::test_copy_enc[sse-kms-unencrypted-STANDARD-STANDARD-1]
s3tests/functional/test_s3.py::test_copy_enc[sse-kms-unencrypted-STANDARD-STANDARD-1024]
s3tests/functional/test_s3.py::test_copy_enc[sse-kms-unencrypted-STANDARD-STANDARD-1048576]
s3tests/functional/test_s3.py::test_copy_enc[sse-kms-unencrypted-STANDARD-STANDARD-8388608]
s3tests/functional/test_s3.py::test_copy_part_enc[sse-kms-unencrypted-STANDARD-STANDARD-8388608]
